newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Islamist reporters charged in prosecutor case.
newsitem.headline: Turk Islamist reporters charged in prosecutor case.

text.p: Three Turkish journalists from an Islamist newspaper face trial after they were alleged to have insulted a prosecutor for his attempts to ban the pro-Islamist Welfare Party, one of the journalists said on Friday.

"A case was opened against me and two of our reporters on Thursday because we criticised the Appeal Court's chief prosecutor in a news story," Ali Ihsan Karahasanoglu, editor of the Akit newspaper, told Reuters.
The prosecutor, Vural Savas, asked the Constitutional Court in May to close Welfare after the party was alleged to have tried to change Turkey's secular system.
Welfare leader Necmettin Erbakan resigned last month after a year as Turkey's first Islamist prime minister. He had been at odds with the country's secular establishment.
Karahasanoglu denied insulting the prosecutor. He said the paper had criticised Savas for holding a news conference about the Welfare case.
The three could be jailed for more than a year each if found guilty, Anatolian news agency said.
